record.final_answer:
**The total shipping cost for October is 58.01.**

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |
| **Total** | | **58.01** |

The script failed on its first run with `no rate for zone "north"`. That's because `data/zone-rates.tsv` has Windows (CRLF) line endings, so the zone names it stores end in a hidden `\r` and never match the order data. To get the result, I gave the script a copy of the rates with those characters removed: `sh scripts/cost.sh data/orders-2026-10.tsv <(tr -d '\r' < data/zone-rates.tsv)`. The script and both data files are unchanged.

You may want to convert `zone-rates.tsv` to Unix line endings at some point, or have the script strip `\r`, so it works without the workaround. I've saved this issue in memory so a later session will know about it.
